subject: economics
chapter_title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and Its Neighbours

concepts.title: Development Path and Reform Timelines of India, China and Pakistan
concepts.definition: India, China and Pakistan started development around the same time with planning and public sector roles; China began reforms in 1978, Pakistan in 1988 and India in 1991, with China following a state-led command model before market reforms and special economic zones.
concepts.key_idea: Comparing the three neighbours shows how different reform timings and strategies produced different growth outcomes.

solution_steps.explain: Separate command, mixed and reform strategies.

concepts.title: Human Development and Demographic Indicators Compared
concepts.definition: The three countries are compared on indicators like GDP growth rate, infant mortality rate, maternal mortality rate, literacy rate, life expectancy, population below poverty line and the human development index, with China leading on most health and mortality indicators and Pakistan lagging on literacy and poverty.
concepts.key_idea: China's one child policy lowered population growth, while India and Pakistan show higher population growth rates that dilute per capita gains.

solution_steps.explain: Choose mortality, literacy, HDI or poverty measure.

concepts.title: Conclusions: Sectoral Shares, Employment and Lessons
concepts.definition: China has the largest share of workforce in industry and the highest GDP growth, India leads in services with strong engineering and IT exports, Pakistan depends more on agriculture and remittances, and the comparative study warns that development requires attention to health, education and balanced sectoral growth.
concepts.key_idea: The lesson is that policy stability, human development investment and export orientation together decide development success.
